habit_scope: current volume habit — 54% of new-home framed floor area (HUD RSDG §1.3, APA 2013). Install per manufacturer ESR (filed from PJI/ESR-1262 as Source; CLASS is I-joist).
how_it_is_done: Sill/anchors on the cured wall (AF&PA Sills; ORNL notes 11, 13, 31, 34 gasket). I-joists never remain in direct contact with concrete or masonry (PJI Note 5) — sill/plate or hanger separates them (D10 / c-P07-D10-bearing-split).

Girders: built-up, steel W house beam, or EWP (AF&PA Beams; HUD §5.4.3). Steel house beam is a girder alternate with a bolted 2x cap for nailing (HUD) — not a floor habit. Bar joists rejected. Built-up nailing D5: keep both AF&PA 20d/32 and HUD 10d/12; do not mix on one beam; follow NDS/IRC (c-P07-D5-girder-nailing). Bearing ≥4 in (AF&PA).

Set I-joists. End bearing ≥1¾ in; intermediate ≥3½ in (PJI Notes 5–6). Do not use sawn 1½ in under I-joists (D10). Crown/orientation per the guide. Cut to length only. Never cut, drill, or notch flanges (PJI p 3 / Notes).

I-joist-only hold: brace each joist as it is set; temporary 1x4 struts ≤8 ft o.c. before anyone walks; sheath before stacking; stack only over walls/beams (PJI p 3). Sawn books do not impose this hold.

Rim/band or APA rim / blocking panels. Rollover restraint is mandatory (PJI Note 7). Interior bearing walls: full-depth blocking or squash blocks; walls aligned story-to-story (PJI 1g). I-joist blocking is stability and load transfer, not the old sawn-bridging stiffness argument (D3).
Openings: hangers + backer/filler (PJI 1h–1m). Hangers ICC-ES recognized; web stiffeners when the hanger does not brace the top flange or when tables require them (PJI p 13).

Web holes per the manufacturer table (PJI pp 17–18 / Table 9): never flange; max hole = web clear minus 1/4 in; ≤3 max-size holes per span; prefer knockouts; rectangular corners pre-drilled. Do not mix with sawn notch/hole rules.

Subfloor: panels long way across supports, ≥2 spans, ~1/8 in gap (AF&PA Sub-flooring). Glue is required for PJI catalog spans (APA AFG-01 / ASTM D3498). Nail-only I-joist floors: drop spacing to 12 in o.c. (PJI table note). L/480 residential tables (PJI; HUD notes manufacturers use L/480 above 15 ft). Fastener grid 6 in edge / 12 in field (HUD Table 5.5).

Shop drawings / ESR on site (HUD §1.3, §5.4). Never repair a damaged I-joist in the field (PJI — rejected as a process). Floor framing PRECEDES significant basement backfill (HUD §4.5); can_overlap false on that hold.
trades: framing subcontractors (AF&PA names subcontractors / job foreman / inspector — no crew size)
tools_equipment: Named in PJI: crane lift in supplier bundles, webs vertical, pick at fifth-points, spreader if needed; never twist or load a joist on its side. Temporary 1x4 struts. ICC-ES hangers matched to flange width. Not a full tool inventory.
inspection_hold_points: Grade-marked / ESR product on site (AF&PA grade-mark family; HUD §1.3 shop drawings/ESR).
Brace before walk; no stack on unsheathed joists (PJI p 3).
No flange cuts; holes only as tabled; stiffeners when required (PJI Notes 1–13).
Sheathing glue on if using catalog spans (PJI).
Bearing 1¾ / 3½; not on bare concrete (PJI Notes 5–6; D10).
Floor in before significant basement backfill (HUD §4.5).
material_classes_notes: Never PowerJoist, Anthony, or other brand names in material_classes. Brand lives only on src-pji-guide / scribd_sources.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the current volume habit for framed floors (HUD §1.3 APA 2013 54%). Beats sawn on span, straightness, and catalog L/480 floors when glue and ESR are followed. Does not apply on Southern SOG (c-P07-no-joists-on-sog).
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: SOG South / Fontana — no joist package. Never on bare concrete. Nail-only with catalog spans (must drop to 12 in o.c.). Mixing sawn 1½-in bearing or sawn hole rules. Field-repairing a damaged joist (PJI: never). Logan roof snow is P09 except girder loads later (mn-logan).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did learn it if they frame new SFR volume — it is the 54% habit. What they skip is brace-before-walk, glue-for-catalog-spans, and no-flange-cut.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: I-joist layout / ESR on drawings before permit. Engineer when tables fail (HUD). Good first offer: I-joist vs sawn is a permit-gate framing choice — catch before permit.
risk_if_swapped_late: Swapping I-joist vs sawn after permit changes spans, hangers, rim, glue spec, and hole rules. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: These are the I-joists most new houses use. Sit them on a sill, not on bare concrete. Brace each one before anybody walks. Do not cut the flange. Glue the deck if you are using the catalog spans — nail-only means 12 inch on center. Keep the manufacturer sheet on site. Not for a Fontana slab house.
spanish_summary: Estas son las viguetas en I que usa la mayoría de casas nuevas. Van sobre solera, nunca sobre concreto pelado. Se arriostran antes de caminar. No se corta el patín. El pegamento del piso es obligatorio si usa las tablas de claro; solo clavo baja a 12 pulgadas. La ficha del fabricante en la obra. No aplica en losa de Fontana.
